insights.headline: Russia's record gold sell-off and CIBC's forecast cuts top a busy day for India buyers
insights.summary: Russia sold about 62 tonnes of gold since December 2025, its biggest reserve drawdown since 1998, as the Kremlin covers a widening budget deficit. CIBC cut its gold forecasts — $4,500 for Q4 2026 and a $5,200 average for 2027 — blaming a stronger dollar and a more hawkish Fed. In India, the World Gold Council says seasonal demand is gaining strength, with domestic discounts narrowing to $8/oz and gold ETF inflows at a seven-month high, while MCX stayed closed for the Dussehra morning session.
points: Russia's gold reserves fell to 72.8 million ounces (2,264 tonnes), the lowest since end-2019, after ten straight months of sales.
CIBC still sees $5,500 gold in 2028, above consensus, on geopolitical risk, fiscal concerns and central-bank buying.
India's September gold imports fell 81% to $1.8bn, while ETF inflows and festive demand strengthened, the World Gold Council says.
Spot gold held near $4,130–4,150; traders price a 91% chance of a December Fed hike as Brent hits a five-month high.
Hindustan Zinc's Q2 profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore as silver output rose 20% to 173 tonnes.

trending.title: Moscow is spending its gold
trending.summary: Russia's 62-tonne reserve drawdown since December — the largest since 1998 — marks a reversal of its pre-war accumulation strategy as the budget deficit heads for 7.3 trillion roubles.

trending.title: Banks are rewriting gold's price path
trending.summary: CIBC's sharp forecast cuts and CPM Group's 'lower first, then breakout' call show the street split between near-term rate pressure and a longer-term recovery story.

trending.title: India's festive demand is stirring early
trending.summary: Narrowing discounts, record ETF inflows and improving store footfall point to early festival-season strength, though high prices keep buyers cautious and selective.

trending.title: The October 27-28 Fed meeting is the market's focal point
trending.summary: Warsh's Bangkok remarks eased October hike fears below 20%, but December hike odds near 90% and five-month-high oil keep bullion capped.

items.title: Russia sells 62 tonnes of gold in biggest reserve drawdown since 1998
items.summary: Bank of Russia data show gold reserves fell another 200,000 troy ounces (6.2 tonnes) in September, to 72.8 million ounces (2,264 tonnes) — the lowest since end-2019. The central bank has cut holdings for ten straight months, disposing of about 62 tonnes since December 2025, as the Kremlin covers a widening budget deficit; the Finance Ministry expects the 2026 deficit to reach 7.3 trillion roubles.

items.title: CIBC slashes gold price forecasts, still sees $5,500 in 2028
items.summary: In its October outlook, CIBC cut its Q4 2026 gold forecast to $4,500 an ounce from $6,500, its 2027 average to $5,200 from $6,500 and its 2028 estimate to $5,500 from $6,000. The bank cites higher energy prices, a stronger dollar and a more hawkish Fed; it also cut its 2027 silver forecast to $85 an ounce from $120.

items.title: World Gold Council: India's seasonal gold demand shows early strength
items.summary: The World Gold Council's India market update says domestic gold price discounts narrowed sharply in October, from an average of $66/oz in September to $8/oz as of 16 October, as seasonal demand gathered pace. Gold ETF net inflows hit a seven-month high in September at Rs 44.5 billion, with Rs 17.22 billion more in the first half of October.

items.title: Gold eases as elevated oil prices keep inflation risks in focus
items.summary: Reuters reported spot gold fell 0.4% to $4,123.94 an ounce on Tuesday as firmer oil prices — Brent near a five-month high after Houthi attacks on Saudi targets — heightened inflation concerns. Recent Fed comments have tempered expectations of an October hike, but traders still see a 91% chance of a December increase; spot silver rose 0.2% to $57.20.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: Gold above Rs 1,47,000, silver near Rs 2.10 lakh on Dussehra
items.summary: IANS reports that MCX stayed closed for the morning session on Dussehra, with trading set to resume at 5 pm. In Monday's session, December gold futures settled down Rs 618 at Rs 1,47,300 per 10 grams while December silver futures closed flat at Rs 2,09,825 per kg; 24-karat gold in Mumbai was Rs 1,47,340. Spot gold edged up to $4,144.15 and silver to $57.44.

items.title: Silver Surplus Calls May Overstate the Impact of Weaker Solar Demand
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and StoneX have shifted to surplus language - a possible physical silver surplus in 2027, or a 2026 surplus of about five weeks of demand (~107 Moz). Przemyslaw Radomski argues the solar decline is largely already counted: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute already assume PV demand falls 19% to 151 Moz inside a 46.3 Moz 2026 shortfall.

items.title: Gold, silver rise on MCX as Fed rate hike odds drop below 20%
items.summary: December MCX gold futures rose 0.31% to Rs 1,48,379 per 10 grams and silver 0.39% to Rs 2,12,013 per kg in early trade on 19 October, after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks in Bangkok cut the implied chance of an October hike below 20%. December remains in play with hot producer-price data; the 27-28 October FOMC meeting is the next key test, and a firmer rupee is capping domestic gains.

items.title: CPM Group's Jeff Christian: lower first, then a breakout for gold and silver
items.summary: CPM Group's Jeffrey Christian expects gold and silver prices to rise over the next several months despite near-term pressure, with silver seen breaking out of its range to the upside in two to three months. Gold futures have been testing $4,100 while silver repeatedly tests $60; gold ETFs added about 3 million ounces in August and 2 million in September, and central bank buying continues.

items.title: India's festive and wedding season demand picks up as prices ease
items.summary: Jewellers report improving footfall as the festive and wedding season begins, with manufacturers seeing strong orders and buyers favouring lighter designs and old-gold exchange deals, which rose over 10%. Gold slipped about 5% in India in September, and listed jewellers posted 20-30% revenue growth in the July-September quarter.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.
